payload.headline: NVIDIA at 155.46 as results land amid reported CEO exit; hold, wait

summary.thesis: The business is still growing fast, with rising margins and a large cash flow, and the price assumes less growth than recent results show, but governance problems and a downtrend cloud the picture.
summary.decision: Hold the shares without adding until the filed third-quarter figures confirm margins and customer payments, and make no swing trade until the market has reacted to the report.
summary.act_at: Add at 150.22 if the filing confirms margins; trim near 218.73

payload.happening: NVIDIA closed at 155.46, down 0.44% on the day and in a downtrend, below its 20-day (192.59), 50-day (211.75) and 200-day (203.6) averages. Third-quarter fiscal 2027 results came out after the close, confirmed by an 8-K filing. The Verge reported that they 'hit the mark', but the figures are not in our data yet. The same day, outlets reported that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO and says he is open to returning. They also reported a DOJ investigation into Megaspeed, a company the FT links to the Huang family.
payload.business: What changes the business: demand and margins were strong as of the last filed quarter. Sales grew 105.85% over a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 127.0B over twelve months, up from 72.0B. The company holds 23.2B more cash than debt. Two numbers put this at risk. First, unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Second, the 65% margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%, and margins that high tend to come down. The FT reported that NVIDIA stopped disclosing its Singapore sales, which makes it harder to see where demand comes from. The FT also reported that newer chipmakers see an opening, though that is a sentiment story until it shows up in sales. What changes mostly sentiment and governance: the reported CEO exit, the reported DOJ probe of Megaspeed, and insider sales of $946.6M made outside pre-set plans. These do not change today's cash or margins. They could matter for the business if they affect customers, export permissions or how quickly the company makes decisions (general knowledge). The cash position and the current profit level are not at risk today. The pace of future growth and how much investors trust management are.

worth.text: The price of 155.46 implies that free cash flow starts growing at about 20.9% a year and slows from there. On that model, 20% starting growth is worth 150.22 a share, 30% is worth 218.73 and 0% is worth 68.05. Recent growth has been much faster: sales grew 83% last year and 110% a year over three years. That is why the discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 189.87 in its bear case, 220.46 in its base case and 261.33 in its bull case. All three are above the price. By the company's own history of price-to-sales (share price compared with sales), the range is 217.35 to 411.04, and the current price-to-sales of 12.4 sits at the 4.0 percentile of its last five years. Peers trade at a median of 15.7. The earnings multiples are also low: 19.6 times trailing earnings, 16.7 times this year's estimate and 9.8 times next year's. The gap between methods comes from one assumption: whether growth and margin hold up. If operating margin falls to 48%, the value drops to 112.91. At 32% it drops to 75.59. Given the warning on customer bills and the governance news, the range here is held at the cautious end, from 20% to 30% starting growth.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near 65.21% rather than fading toward 48%.

bull: Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and twelve-month free cash flow grew to 127.0B from 72.0B.
The shares trade at 9.8 times next year's estimated earnings and 12.4 times sales, below the peer median of 15.7 and at the 4.0 percentile of their own 5-year history.
Analysts raised next year's EPS estimate by 23.2% over 90 days, and even the cautious DCF case (189.87) is above the 155.46 price.
bear: Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, a sign that sales may have been pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly.
If operating margin falls from its 5-year peak to 48%, the model value drops to 112.91, well below today's price.
Governance risk is rising: insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans, the CEO's exit was reported, and outlets reported a DOJ investigation into Megaspeed.

levels.what: Today's close. It implies about 20.9% starting cash-flow growth, below what recent results have delivered, which is enough to keep holding but not enough to add before the filed numbers are in.
The value at 20% starting growth, sitting just above the 147.59–150.01 support zone. Add here only if the filing shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
The value at 30% starting growth, close to the DCF base of 220.46. Near this price most of the upside is used up, so trim there.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee call is 'Hold', and the macro, technical and risk views are all negative. The value supports owning the stock. The customer-bill warning, the governance reports and unreleased figures argue against adding yet.

swing.why: The report came out after the close, and options price a 9.7% move by 2026-11-20, more than one average daily range (ATR 9.71). A stop under the 147.59–150.01 support could be skipped by a price gap, and the first resistance at 163.9–169.14 leaves little room to the upside.

decision.timing: Take no action until the market has reacted to the 2026-11-17 report. Options imply 103.6 volatility against 53.8 realized, a ratio of 1.92, so a large move is expected. When the figures are out, compare revenue with 108.7B, EPS with 2.47 and next-quarter guidance with 124.9B before acting at 150.22 or 218.73.

change_mind: If the filed quarter shows revenue below the 108.7B consensus or guidance below 124.9B, the 20.9% growth the price implies looks less safe; move from hold to wait.
If the price closes below the 147.59–150.01 support zone, the hold case weakens and the next valuation marker is the 48%-margin value of 112.91; no adding until that is resolved.

If the filing shows operating margin back near 58.09% or lower, or customer bills again growing faster than sales, cut the range toward 112.91; if margin holds near 65.21% with bills in line, add at 150.22.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold and no swing trade, because the 8-K results landed after the close but their figures are not yet in our data, and the price of 155.46 still implies about 20.9% growth, between the 150.22 and 218.73 marks.
